hypothesis.title: payment 1.9.1 rollout throws TypeError on charge.js:41 reading 'units'
hypothesis.summary: Payment service was deployed from 1.9.0 to 1.9.1 eleven minutes before the alert. The new version introduced a TypeError in charge.js:41 attempting to read 'units' from an undefined object, causing 40% of payment requests to fail. These errors propagate upstream to checkout, triggering the CheckoutHighErrorRate alert with 36% errors. This matches a known pattern from PM-2026-01-20 where payment code incorrectly assumed amount.units was always present.
hypothesis.reasoning: The alert fired on checkout with a 36% error rate. Examining the trace evidence, 99% of failing checkout traces end in payment (68 out of 69 failures). The deepest error in the failing traces is "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'units') at charge.js:41" originating from payment. Payment's own error rate spiked from 0.4% to 40.4%, and payment logs show 818 occurrences of this exact TypeError starting 11 minutes before the alert. Payment was deployed from version 1.9.0 to 1.9.1 exactly 11 minutes before the alert, and the error logs first appeared at the same time (-11m). This matches postmortem PM-2026-01-20, which describes an identical TypeError in payment 1.7.3 caused by a code change that assumed amount.units was always set. The frontend-proxy deployment 22 minutes before the alert is a red herring—it occurred 11 minutes before the payment errors started, and frontend-proxy is not on the failing call path from checkout to payment. Payment's CPU and memory are stable, ruling out resource saturation. The root cause is the bad deploy of payment 1.9.1.

supporting_evidence.why_it_matters: Payment rolled out version 1.9.1 exactly 11 minutes before the alert, coinciding with the start of the error spike.
818 TypeError logs in payment starting at -11m (deployment time) with the exact error 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading units) at charge.js:41'.
99% of failing checkout traces (68/69) terminate with errors in payment, proving payment is the origin not a victim.
Payment error rate jumped from 0.4% to 40.4% at -10m, immediately after the 1.9.1 deployment, showing the new version is faulty.
Example failing trace shows the deepest error originates in payment span with the same TypeError, confirming payment is the root cause.
Checkout logs 718 errors calling payment with the same TypeError, confirming errors propagate from payment to checkout.

suggested_actions.title: Rollback payment deployment to version 1.9.0
suggested_actions.rationale: The 1.9.1 deployment introduced the TypeError. Rolling back to the last known good version (1.9.0) will immediately stop the errors. This matches the resolution in PM-2026-01-20.

suggested_actions.title: Verify payment error rate returns to baseline after rollback
suggested_actions.command: kubectl logs -n otel-demo -l app=payment --tail=50 | grep -i error
suggested_actions.rationale: Confirm that the TypeError stops appearing in payment logs and error rate drops below 5% within 2-3 minutes of the rollback.

suggested_actions.title: Review payment 1.9.1 code changes in charge.js around line 41
suggested_actions.rationale: Identify the code change that assumes amount.units exists. The bug likely mirrors PM-2026-01-20 where the code did not handle clients sending amount.nanos only. Fix and add tests before re-releasing.

alternatives.why_less_likely: Frontend-proxy deployed 22 minutes before the alert, but payment errors started only 11 minutes before (coinciding with payment's own deploy). Frontend-proxy is not on the checkout→payment call path, and there is no evidence of frontend-proxy causing the specific TypeError in payment's charge.js.

retrieved_documents.title: CrashLoopBackOff triage
retrieved_documents.snippet: 1. `kubectl -n otel-demo logs <pod> --previous` shows why the last start failed. 2. Missing env var / config file / bad command -> check the most recent config change or rollout. 3. If a rollout caused it: `kubectl -n otel-demo rollout undo deployment/<svc>`. 4. If an env var changed: restore it with `kubectl set env`.
